name: Car repair and service garage
description: A car repair and service garage: the services, a price list and customers' questions, with facts about the brands serviced, the labour rate, the warranty on work, a courtesy car and the periodic vehicle inspection.

questions.question: Which car brands do you service?
questions.help: For example "all brands, specialised in Toyota and VW". Say "authorised service" only if a manufacturer has actually authorised you.

questions.question: What is your hourly labour rate?
questions.help: An amount with the currency; say in the price list whether VAT is included.

questions.question: What warranty do you give on repairs and parts?
questions.help: For example "12 months on labour, parts as the supplier". Check the minimum your law requires.

questions.question: Can customers get a courtesy car while theirs is in the garage? On what terms?
questions.help: For example "yes, free for repairs over one day, book it in advance" or "no".

questions.question: Do you carry out the periodic roadworthiness inspection, or take cars to it for customers?
questions.help: Use the name customers in your country know (MOT, STK, TÜV/HU, §57a…), e.g. "pre-inspection check and we take the car to the inspection station".

questions.question: Since which year has the garage been running?

audit.message: Add the services you offer – servicing, repairs, tyres, diagnostics – each with what it includes.
The price list has not changed for a year – check the labour rate and the prices of common jobs.
Say which brands you service – drivers check this before they book.
Add your opening hours in Business details – customers plan when to drop the car off.
Fill in your phone number in Business details – most customers call to book or ask about their car.

claude: Drivers want to know whether the garage handles their car and the job, what it roughly costs, when they can come and whether they can get a courtesy car – put the services, brands, opening hours and a way to book at the top. When the Bookings feature is on, set up the usual jobs as booking services and place a Booking element on the booking page; when it is off, lead with the phone and an enquiry form. Write plainly, like a mechanic explaining the job. Prices are "from" with the final price after diagnosis; never invent prices, the labour rate, warranty terms, brand authorisations ("authorised service" only when the owner confirms it), certifications or reviews, and use manufacturers' logos only if the owner may. Inspection rules and names differ by country (MOT, STK, TÜV) – word them neutrally and say that legal details should be checked.
